problem:
$$
D=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 5 \\ -9 & -6 & -6 \\ -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

If $D=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $D$ given above, what is the value of ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{23}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062864/assets/e819307ecef66a628ff3b0b03d98c6e0f054bbb6c78cd9e7395b99e45f54000a.png)

If $A=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ given above, what is the value of $l_{31} \cdot u_{23}?$
examples.worked_solution:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & 1 \\ -6 & 3 & -12 \\ -4 & 10 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & 1 \\ -3 & 24 & -9 \\ -4 & 10 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & 1 \\ -3 & 24 & -9 \\ -2 & 24 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & 1 \\ -3 & 24 & -9 \\ -2 & \,1\, & 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062864/assets/1ae6992336eda022f30a643ff0e89ae46c37978ac193370e518ecbea5084878b.png)

Finally, since $l_{31}=-2$ and $u_{23}=-9,$ we get

$$
l_{31} \cdot u_{23} = (-2) \cdot (-9) =18.
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 \\ 18 & -1 & 3 \\ -6 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ \boxed{} & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}
$$

Consider the LU factorization of the matrix $A$ above. What is the value of the entry ${l}_{31}$ in the matrix $L?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We want to make $0$ at the position ${a}_{31}$ using Gaussian elimination. To do this, we take the $3$rd row of $A,$ and we add the $1$st row of $A$ multiplied by $-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 \\ 18 & -1 & 3 \\ -6 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 \\ 18 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The entry ${l}_{31}$ of the matrix $L$ is the factor next to ${R}_{1},$ taken with the opposite sign:

$$
{l}_{31}=-(-1)=1.
$$
